Macrons

Consonantal i

Kitchen, meals & drinks

no, thank you phrase

also have some more, enough

classical

benignē

adverb

Here benignē is a polite refusal.

Examples

  • Vēscere, sōdēs. — Jam satis est. — At tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — Benignē.

    Eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Take as much as you like. — No, thank youHor. Epist. I 7, 15–16

  • Īte domum saturae, venit Hesperus.

    Go home full, the evening star is coming (said after the meal)Verg. Ecl. 10, 77

See also be hungry.

SourcesLewis & Short: benigne · Lewis & Short: vescor

These are quotations, and their sources are given. Libellī II and IV and the back-matter lists of “locī memoriā tenendī” suggest when to use them with Theo.
